Spec review companion · #110 · snapshot 19c92e8 · 2026-10-27

Skip untracked files behind a directory junction on Windows

Read the open sections in about ten minutes. Everything closed is a look-up. A file:line chip jumps to the source line at the bottom, for when a claim needs checking.

Bug #110

The change

On Windows, a review read an untracked file that lies outside the repo when a directory junction in the repo pointed at it. Git for Windows lists the files behind a junction, and each such file is a plain file, so its text went into the prompt and into untracked.md. assessment:21

The fix also skips an untracked file whose real path is outside the repo or in a .git folder, with the same (skipped: symlink) note. fix:10

3code and doc files (git.mjs, README, CHANGELOG), plus 4 version files fix:19 fix:24
7tests added fix:68
7checks passed test:7
0checks failed test:7
3deviations fix:78

Root cause

formatUntrackedFile checks whether the leaf is a link, not whether its real path is inside the repo. assessment:52

Remediation

Compare the real path of the file with that of the root, after the leaf check; all three callers use this one function. assessment:60

# Bug Assessment: a review reads an untracked file behind a directory junction, outside the repo - **Slug**: 110-skip-files-behind-junction- **Created**: 2026-10-27- **Source**: pasted text (GitHub issue #110)- **Verdict**: valid- **Severity**: high ## Report (verbatim or summarized) Summarized from #110. On Windows, a review reads a file that lies outside the repo when a directoryjunction inside the repo points at it. `formatUntrackedFile`(`plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs`) runs `lstat` on the leaf path only. Git for Windowsdescends into a junction and lists `linkdir/key.txt` as untracked; the leaf is a plain file, so itstext goes into the prompt and into `untracked.md`. A junction needs no privilege to create. TheREADME and the `git.mjs` header say a review never reads the target of an untracked link, which isfalse on Windows. On macOS and Linux git lists a symlinked directory as one entry and does notdescend into it. The issue asks that a review never read a file whose real path is outside the reporoot, with a skip note, on every platform, with tests, a README line and a patch release. ## Symptom On Windows, a working-tree review of a repo with an untracked directory junction that pointsoutside the repo puts the text of the files behind the junction into the prompt (inline) and into`untracked.md` (above the inline limit). Expected: such a file is skipped with a note, as anuntracked file link is today. ## Reproduction Reproduced on 2026-10-27 on Windows with the code on `main` (18527bc), from a Node script outsidethe repo: 1. Make a temp folder with `outside/key.txt` (text `SECRET_OUTSIDE_MARKER`) and a repo `repo/` with   one commit.2. Create `repo/linkdir` as a directory junction to `outside`   (`fs.symlinkSync(outside, link, "junction")`).3. `getWorkingTreeState(repo).untracked` is `["linkdir/key.txt"]`.4. `collectReviewContext(repo, resolveReviewTarget(repo, {})).content` contains   `SECRET_OUTSIDE_MARKER`. ## Suspected Code Paths - `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs:234-266` (`formatUntrackedFile`): `lstat` of the leaf only;  the leaf behind a junction is a plain file, so it is read.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs:277` and `:287` (`collectWorkingTreeContext`, inline and  lightweight context) and `:418` (`writeReviewPatches`, `untracked.md`): the three callers, all  with the repo root as `cwd`.- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs:1-5` (header) and `README.md:294` ("Differences from the  Codex plugin"): the claim that a review never reads the target of an untracked link.- `tests/git.test.mjs:508` covers a file link only. ## Root Cause Hypothesis `formatUntrackedFile` checks whether the leaf itself is a link, not whether its real path is insidethe repo. A directory junction makes the leaf a plain file whose real path is outside, and Git forWindows lists files behind it. Confidence: high (reproduced). ## Proposed Remediation **Preferred**: in `formatUntrackedFile`, keep the leaf-link check, and inside the same `try` alsotake `fs.realpathSync.native` of the file and of the repo root (`cwd`). When`rel = path.relative(realRoot, realFile)` is `""`, is `..`, starts with `..` followed by`path.sep`, or is absolute (another drive), return `### <path>\n(skipped: symlink)`, the note afile link gets today. A bare `startsWith("..")` would also skip an in-repo name such as`..notes.txt`. Order: the leaf-link check first (a file link keeps its note), then the real-pathcheck, then the directory and size checks. A failed `realpath` gives the existing "broken symlinkor unreadable file" note. All three callers use this function, so thecontext and `untracked.md` are both covered. Update the header comment. **Alternatives**:- `lstat` every path component: more calls, and the real-path check also covers a junction in any  folder above the file inside the repo. **Files likely to change**:- `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs`- `tests/git.test.mjs`, `tests/runtime-review-safety.test.mjs`- `README.md` ("Differences from the Codex plugin")- `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` and the version files (`npm run bump-version -- 1.0.22`) **Tests to add or update**:- `tests/git.test.mjs`: a temp folder with `outside/key.txt` (a marker) and a repo with `linkdir`  and `sub/linkdir`, directory junctions on Windows and directory symlinks elsewhere, plus an  ordinary untracked file in a real subfolder and one named `..notes.txt` in the root. For the  inline context and for the lightweight context (`maxInlineFiles`), and for the files that  `writeReviewPatches` writes: the marker is in none of them, and the ordinary files' text is. On  Windows the test also checks the note `### linkdir/key.txt\n(skipped: symlink)`; elsewhere git  lists `linkdir` as one link, which gets the same note under its own name.- A sibling folder whose name starts with the repo's name (`repo` and `repo2`): a junction to  `repo2` is still outside, so `path.relative` and not a string prefix decides.- A junction or directory link that points inside the repo: on Windows its files are read (they are  inside); elsewhere git lists the link itself, which the leaf check skips.- The real-path branch on every platform: `fs.realpathSync.native` mocked (as the existing  `fs.lstatSync` mock test does) so that a plain untracked file resolves outside the repo: the file  is skipped with the symlink note and not read. On Windows only, a mock that resolves it to another  drive (an absolute `path.relative`) gives the same note. Each mock matches the exact unresolved  path it gets (the file's `path.join(root, name)`, or the root) and passes every other path to the  real function.- `fs.realpathSync.native` mocked to throw, once for the file and once for the root, after the stat  checks pass: the "broken symlink or unreadable file" note, and the file is not read, in the inline  context, the lightweight context and the files that `writeReviewPatches` writes.- `tests/runtime-review-safety.test.mjs`: with the fake copilot CLI, a review inline and one above  the inline limit. The marker is in neither the prompt nor any patch file the CLI captured. The  exact skip note is in the inline prompt, and in the captured `untracked.md` above the limit. On  macOS and Linux this test passes on the current code too (git lists the link itself), so there it  guards against a regression; on POSIX the mocked tests above are the ones that fail before the  fix. The companion runs in a child process, where `fs` cannot be mocked, so the acceptance item  "a test proves it on Windows and POSIX with the fake copilot CLI" is met in full on Windows and,  on POSIX, only as that regression guard plus the in-process mocked tests.- The `git.mjs` header (lines 2-3) and the README bullet (lines 294-295) name directory links and  junctions, and say that a review reads no file whose real path is outside the repo. **Checks**: `npm ci --include=dev`, `npm run build`, `npm test`, `npm run check-version` and`claude plugin validate .` must pass before the PR; CI runs the tests on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows. ## Risks & Considerations - On macOS and Linux, git lists a symlinked directory as one link, which the leaf check already  skips. So a real junction reaches the new real-path branch only on Windows (here and in CI); the  mocked `realpathSync.native` tests run that branch on every platform. A dangling junction lists  no file behind it, and a junction to a parent of the repo makes git walk a loop, so neither is a  test case.- A repo whose root is itself reached through a link: both sides are real paths, so files inside  the repo still count as inside.- One more `realpath` per untracked file (and one of the root): small next to reading the file.- Accepted: a path that someone swaps for a link between the `realpath` check and the read is not  covered; that needs a process working in the repo during the review, as for the existing leaf  check.- A file inside the repo reached through an inner junction is read: its real path is inside, so it  holds nothing from outside.- The difference from upstream (Codex reads such a file) goes in the README bullet, which now  speaks of a file whose real path is outside the repo, and names directory links and junctions. ## Open Questions None. ## Constitution Check - **I. Upstream parity**: met. Function and note names stay; the change is a correctness and safety  difference, recorded in the README section "Differences from the Codex plugin" and the `git.mjs`  header comment.- **II. Only reviewed code**: met. Node's `fs.realpathSync.native` and `path.relative`; no new  dependency.- **III. Copilot CLI through documented interfaces only**: met. No change to how Copilot is called.- **IV. Safe by default**: met; this is the point of the fix. A review reads no file whose real path  is outside the repo; nothing is written.- **V. Cross-platform**: met. The test makes a junction on Windows and a directory symlink  elsewhere; CI runs Ubuntu, macOS and Windows.- **VI. Tested, including failure paths**: met. Junction and directory-link cases (also nested), a  sibling-prefix folder, an inner link, a `..notes.txt` file, a mocked outside real path and another  drive, a failed `realpath`, inline and above-limit contexts, the patch files, and a runtime review  with the fake CLI. Patch release with its `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and the release run after the merge.

# Bug Fix: a review reads an untracked file behind a directory junction, outside the repo - **Slug**: 110-skip-files-behind-junction- **Fixed**: 2026-10-27- **Assessment**: ./assessment.md- **Status**: applied ## Summary `formatUntrackedFile` now also skips an untracked file whose real path is outside the repo or in a`.git` folder, after the leaf-link check: it compares `fs.realpathSync.native` of the file with thatof the repo root. A file behind a directory junction (or any folder link) that leads there gets`(skipped: symlink)`, in the inline context, the lightweight context and `untracked.md`. ## Changes | File | Change | Notes ||------|--------|-------|| `plugins/copilot/scripts/lib/git.mjs` | modified | `isOutsideWorkTree` helper (first path part `..`, any part `.git` in any case, an absolute path, or `""`); real-path check in `formatUntrackedFile` after the leaf check, in the same `try`; header comment || `tests/git.test.mjs` | added tests | Real junctions or folder links (outside, nested, sibling `repo2`, inner, `.git`), `..notes.txt`; mocked `realpathSync.native` (outside, a `.git` folder as `.git`, `.GIT` and nested, another drive on Windows, a throw for the file and for the root); three helpers || `tests/runtime-review-safety.test.mjs` | added test | A review with the fake copilot CLI, inline and above the inline limit || `README.md` | modified | The "Differences from the Codex plugin" bullet: no untracked file whose real path is outside the repo or in a `.git` folder, also behind a folder link or a junction || `plugins/copilot/CHANGELOG.md` | modified | `### 1.0.22` entry || `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `plugins/copilot/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | modified | `npm run bump-version -- 1.0.22` | ## Diff Highlights (optional) ```jsfunction isOutsideWorkTree(root, file) {  const relative = path.relative(root, file);  const parts = relative.split(path.sep);  return (    relative === "" ||    parts[0] === ".." ||    parts.some((part) => part.toLowerCase() === ".git") ||    path.isAbsolute(relative)  );}// in formatUntrackedFile, inside the existing try:isLink =  fs.lstatSync(absolutePath).isSymbolicLink() ||  isOutsideWorkTree(fs.realpathSync.native(cwd), fs.realpathSync.native(absolutePath));``` ## Tests Added or Updated - `tests/git.test.mjs` "an untracked file behind a folder link or junction that leads outside the  repo or into .git is not read": `linkdir` and `sub/linkdir` to an outside folder, `siblink` to  `repo2`, `innerlink` to a folder inside, `gitlink` to `.git` (whose config holds a marker); the  inline context, the lightweight context and `untracked.md` hold no outside or `.git` marker and  do hold the inside files (`sub/plain.txt`, `..notes.txt`, `inner/ok.txt`, `.github/ci.yml`,  `.gitattributes`). On Windows the skip notes name the files behind the junctions, and the file  behind the inner junction is read; elsewhere the links themselves are skipped.- "an untracked file whose real path is outside the repo is skipped as a symlink" (mocked  `realpathSync.native`; runs the new branch on every platform).- "an untracked file whose real path is in a .git folder, in any case, is skipped as a symlink"  (mocked: `.git`, `.GIT` and `vendor/lib/.git`, on every platform).- "an untracked file whose real path is on another drive is skipped as a symlink" (Windows only).- "an untracked file whose real path cannot be read for the file / for the repo root is skipped as  unreadable" (two tests).- `tests/runtime-review-safety.test.mjs` "a review sends Copilot no file behind a folder link or  junction that leads outside the repo": the inline prompt has the exact skip note and no marker;  above the inline limit, `untracked.md` has the note, and no captured patch file or the prompt has  the marker. ## Local Verification - With `main`'s `git.mjs` put back for a moment (run again after review round 3), the six new  `git.test.mjs` tests and the runtime test fail on Windows; with the fix, all pass.- The reproduction script from `assessment.md` ("Reproduction"): on `main` the marker is in the  context; with the fix it is not.- Commands run (after review round 3): `npm ci --include=dev` (0 vulnerabilities), `npm run build`  (pass), `npm test` (485 tests: 461 pass, 24 skipped, 0 fail), `npm run check-version` (1.0.22),  `claude plugin validate .` (pass). ## Deviations from Assessment - 2026-10-27, review round 1 (`code-review`): a junction to the repo's own `.git` folder still sent  `.git/config` (which can hold a token) to Copilot: its real path is inside the root. The check  now also skips a real path in `<root>/.git`, by its first path part (`isOutsideWorkTree`); the  same first-part test replaces the `..` prefix test. The real-link test adds `gitlink`; the README  bullet, the header and the CHANGELOG name `.git`. The mocked tests now match paths built from  git's root, which can differ from the temp folder (`/var` is `/private/var` on macOS). The root's  `realpath` runs once per untracked file, a small call next to reading the file.- 2026-10-27, review round 2 (Codex, `code-review`): the `.git` test now looks at every path part,  without case: a case-insensitive file system also finds the folder as `.GIT`, and a nested  clone's `.git` (`vendor/lib/.git`) holds a config too. A mocked test covers `.git`, `.GIT` and the  nested folder on every platform; with the `.git` line taken out, it and the real-link test fail.  The POSIX branch of the real-link test also checks the `siblink` and `gitlink` notes.- 2026-10-27, review round 3 (`code-review`): the real-link test also reads `.github/ci.yml` and  `.gitattributes`, names that only start with `.git`; the README says "a `.git` folder"; the  header comment gives the reason for the case-free check (a case-insensitive file system uses a  folder stored as `.GIT`, and `realpath` keeps that case). A Linux folder named `.Git` is skipped  too, which fails closed.- 2026-10-27, PR review (`code-review`): the POSIX branch of the real-link test also checks the  `innerlink` note (a folder link that stays inside is skipped as a link there); CI on macOS and  Ubuntu runs it. ## Follow-ups - Upstream codex-plugin-cc reads untracked symlink targets (the README difference); the junction  case belongs to the same difference.
